name: Kai Vestergaard-Bergqvist
description:
Kai Vestergaard-Bergqvist is one of perhaps thirty certified BCI forensic examiners in GLMZ, and one of the best. His work sits at the intersection of neuroscience, data analysis, and detective work — he reads the data that brain-computer interfaces record, voluntarily or involuntarily, and uses it to reconstruct events, prove identity, establish timelines, and occasionally recover memories the subject themselves has forgotten.

Born to a Swedish-Indian father and Ghanaian mother, Ravi was a neuroscience researcher at the Axiom Institute before the ethical constraints of corporate research drove him into private practice. He discovered that academic rigor applied to investigative work produced results that neither pure scientists nor pure investigators could match. His testimony has been accepted in corporate arbitration courts across Tiers 2-4, and his findings have both convicted and exonerated subjects in cases ranging from theft to murder.

The darkness of his work is cumulative. Every deep scan means spending hours inside someone else's most intimate neural experiences — their fears, their pleasures, their traumas. Ravi has experienced more of other people's lives than most people experience of their own, and it has made him simultaneously more empathetic and more withdrawn. He knows what people are really thinking because he has literally been inside thousands of heads, and that knowledge has made genuine human connection almost impossible for him.
affiliation: Independent — certified BCI forensic examiner, court-recognized expert
location: A sterile clinic-office hybrid on Kessler Row, equipped with neural scanning equipment that costs more than most apartments, near Halsted and Chicago Ave
specialization: BCI forensics — reading neural data trails, memory fragment recovery, cognitive timeline reconstruction
methods: Deep BCI data extraction — recovering deleted memories and experiences from neural storage
Cognitive timeline reconstruction — building a minute-by-minute record of what a subject's BCI recorded
Neural signature analysis — identifying unique brainwave patterns to prove identity or presence
Ambient BCI data collection — gathering involuntary neural emissions from subjects in proximity
Cross-referencing BCI data with environmental sensors for corroborative evidence
notable_cases: Proved a corporate executive was present at a murder scene by recovering ambient BCI data from three witnesses who didn't know they'd recorded anything
Exonerated a wrongly accused dockworker by demonstrating that their BCI memory of the crime had been fabricated — planted by someone with access to neural editing tools
Reconstructed the final 72 hours of a dead man's BCI to identify his killer — the data had been partially corrupted but Ravi recovered enough fragments to build a case
equipment: NeuroScan 4400 — a clinical-grade BCI analysis platform capable of deep memory extraction
Portable neural interface for field work — lower resolution but can read BCI data without clinical setup
Faraday cage built into his office — prevents external interference during sensitive scans
Custom analytical software he wrote himself for pattern-matching neural signatures
Archive of over 40,000 neural signature profiles collected over fifteen years of practice
personality: Ravi is meticulous to the point of obsession and ethical to the point of inconvenience. He will refuse a case if the client wants him to fabricate findings, and he has testified against his own clients when the evidence pointed in a direction they didn't like. He is quiet, methodical, and uncomfortable in social situations — he relates better to data than to people, which is ironic for someone who spends his life literally inside other people's heads. He has developed an unsettling habit of staring at people's temples when they talk, as if he's trying to read their BCI through their skull. He is deeply troubled by the ethical implications of his work and writes lengthy journal entries about consent and cognitive privacy that nobody reads.

story_hooks: During a routine scan, Ravi discovers that a subject's BCI contains memories that don't belong to them — memories of events that haven't happened yet
Someone with neural editing capabilities is planting false memories in witnesses across multiple cases, and Ravi is the only person who can detect the forgeries
A deep scan goes wrong and Ravi becomes trapped in a dead subject's neural data, experiencing their last hours on loop

physical_description.heritage: Predominantly Northern European (92.2%) with subtle phenotypic contributions from Indigenous American (6.3%) and sub-Saharan African (1.5%) ancestry. Northern European base provides cool undertones and angular bone structure, while secondary ancestries introduce gentle warmth and slight complexity to skin and eye coloration. The blend results in a distinctly Nordic appearance with barely perceptible depth—warmth visible primarily in natural light or at close proximity.
physical_description.build: Lean and composed, with the posture of someone who spends most of their time seated at high-resolution neural imaging consoles. Shoulders slightly rounded from years hunched over data. Wiry rather than muscular, with the controlled efficiency of movement that comes from minimal wasted gesture.
physical_description.hair_color: Dark brown with silver threading at the temples
physical_description.hair_style: Swept back neatly, kept short at the sides. Precision-groomed, no affectation
physical_description.eye_color: Cool gray-blue with subtle warm-brown undertones from ancestry blend
physical_description.skin_tone: Fair to light Nordic base with barely-detectable golden warmth beneath the surface, most evident in natural daylight. Indoor pallor dominates his clinic-bound complexion, but the skin maintains slight luminosity rather than true pallor—a quality imparted by the ancestral warmth beneath fair Northern European epidermis.
physical_description.complexion: Clean-shaven with refined, slightly angular features reflecting Northern European bone structure softened minutely by secondary ancestry—cheekbones carry subtle definition rather than sharp prominence. Faint lines around the eyes from years of close work and concentration. Skin maintains even, fair tone with the faintest golden undertone visible in certain light. Expression tends toward neutral observation rather than warmth.
distinguishing_marks: Faint surgical scar on the left temple, approximately 3cm long, where a diagnostic neural interface was installed during his Axiom Institute years — barely visible unless light catches at certain angles
Thin white line across the inner left wrist, partially obscured by his watch, from a research-era accident with equipment
physical_description.visible_augmentations: None visible. All implants are subcutaneous or internal. He wears a discrete neural readout device on his left wrist — a thin, matte-black band that syncs with his clinic equipment, but it appears to be ordinary chronometry to casual observation.
physical_description.posture_movement: Precise, measured movements. He walks with purpose but without aggression. Sits very still during interviews — rarely fidgets, rarely blinks noticeably. Tends to hold eye contact slightly longer than social convention, an occupational habit from reading micro-expressions. Speaks in measured tones with minimal hand gestures.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 2-3 functional minimalism. Favors high-end athleistic wear in muted grays, blacks, and deep blues — brands like Helios and Kasper that advertise durability and precision over ostentation. Wears well-fitted compression shirts under open jackets, functional clothing that suggests athletic maintenance without athletic pretension. His watch is an expensive Swiss-analog piece, a deliberate rejection of smart devices. Minimal jewelry — a simple silver band on his right ring finger, no other adornment. Everything about his appearance is calibrated to project competence and impartiality rather than personality.
